delta_from_prior: Replaces prior 18-variable neon_worstcase_auto_00117 (which compressed and collapsed to peak 1) and extends Neon58 (20 variables, 108 clauses, 16-variable 4x4 quotient, peak 8) to a 22-variable, 150-clause asymmetric 5x4 XOR-lifted bipartite pair-transversal. Unlike Neon58's symmetric 4x4 block frequencies (which interleaved Side A and Side B variables and triggered early elim at depth 4), the 5x4 asymmetry forces compress_root's frequency-first basis sort to place all 10 Side-A quotient variables (frequency 20) ahead of all 8 Side-B quotient variables (frequency 13), with the 5 first-members before the 5 second-members. This drives a predicted peak of 15 incomparable post-elim states at depth 4 (nearly double Neon58's peak 8) while keeping total IALH-5 calls around 65 and avoiding timeout. Also acknowledges the falsification of Neon54/55 K6 near-parity witnesses (peak 0 via global IALH-5 congruences) and audits v5's compression, core_refutation, and residual solver code paths.
explanation:
### 1. Code Audit of Pinned v5 (`blq-composed-core-scc-emra-ialh5-v5`)
Auditing the supplied `run_counting`, `compression.py`, `core_refutation.py`, and pinned SCC/DP/MRA dependencies reveals no soundness bug (no `correctness_fixture`):
- **Supported block identity coverage & quotient partitions (`compression.py`)**: `_verify_certificate` constructs `blocks` from every clause of `dense_formula(formula, ids)`, checks `len(counts) == len(blocks)` and `sum(counts) == len(quotient)`, and for each block checks `any(forms[i] & ~mask for i in indices)` so every quotient coordinate referenced by `q` depends solely on `support`. Checking `evaluate(clauses, x) == evaluate(q, image)` over all `x in points(support)` establishes blockwise equivalence, and conjunction gives global equivalence `F(X) = Q(P(X))`.
- **Right-inverse entries & dense ID mapping**: `right_inverse` computes a GF(2) right inverse `L`, and `_verify_certificate` independently checks `parity(form & column) == int(i == j)` for all `i, j`. This proves surjectivity of `P` without enumerating `2^n` assignments. Dense mapping `ids = sorted(...)` is checked against `cert['variables']`.
- **Exact fallback & core refutation (`core_refutation.py`)**: `probe` checks `set(core).issubset(set(f))` and `core != f`, runs `compress_root(core)` (which invokes `verify_certificate`), and only returns `UNSAT` if the compressed quotient is purely binary (`len(c) <= 2`) and refuted by `two_sat`. Composing `probe` once on an accepted exact quotient preserves soundness. Any `SAT`, non-binary, or budget failure falls back cleanly to exact search.
- **Residual solver (`run_counting_core`, `refute`, `canon_plus`, `elim_plus`, `prune`)**: `refute` builds UP-filtered tables (`up_survives`), computes lattice hulls, and independently checks every local row and the global rational Farkas dual via `Fraction`. `canon_plus`, `elim_plus` (size-nonincreasing DP), and `prune` (subsumption pruning of stronger disjuncts) all preserve satisfiability.

### 2. Acknowledgment of Prior Receipts & Challenge to Untrusted Proposals
- **Prior receipts**: Neon54/55 K6 near-parity witnesses were falsified at peak 0 because width-5 UP tables retain XOR congruences after deleting an extra satisfying point and the global lattice combines rows across windows. `neon_worstcase_auto_00117` compressed cleanly but collapsed to peak 1.
- **Challenge to Fable's ordering / link-twin / fibre-transfer proposals**: The trusted follow-up on Fable73 showed that manually reordering Neon58's 16-variable quotient to pair siblings `[1, 9, 3, 11, ...]` reduced peak 8 to 2, and Fable61/73 proposed list-core selection and nonlinear link-twin contraction. However, (i) `compress_root` has no awareness of nonlinear pair-transversal structure and deterministically outputs quotient variables in `(-block_frequency, popcount, bitmask)` order, which actively separates sibling pairs whenever frequencies or popcounts differ; (ii) any heuristic that only contracts symmetric degree-2/pair-transversal twins or reorders specific bipartite pairs does not bound residual frontier or preprocessing work on general kernel-free CNF (and adds unproved discovery/verification overhead); (iii) a finite peak reduction on one reordered 16-variable instance is not a polynomial-time bound.

### 3. New 22-Variable Growth Fixture: Asymmetric 5x4 XOR-Lifted Bipartite Pair-Transversal
We construct an UNSAT 22-variable, 150-clause formula (max width 7) that **passes exact root compression** (for automatic Lean checking), **evades both original and quotient core refutation**, and drives a **predicted peak of 15** on pinned v5 while keeping total IALH-5 work comparable to Neon58 (~65 calls, avoiding timeout):
- **Quotient structure (18 variables, 68 clauses)**:
  - Side A: 5 disjoint pairs `(a1, a1'), ..., (a5, a5')` with all `2^5 = 32` negative 5-clauses selecting one literal per pair.
  - Side B: 4 disjoint pairs `(b1, b1'), ..., (b4, b4')` with all `2^4 = 16` negative 4-clauses selecting one literal per pair.
  - Positive cross clauses: all `5 * 4 = 20` width-4 clauses `pairA_i U pairB_j`.
  - **UNSAT proof**: Any satisfying assignment must set at least one pair on Side A to `(0, 0)` (else some negative 5-clause on A is falsified) and at least one pair on Side B to `(0, 0)` (else some negative 4-clause on B is falsified), falsifying their positive cross clause.
- **Exact XOR lifting (22 variables, 150 clauses)**:
  - Side A pairs: `(1, 6), (2, 7), (3, 8), (4, 15^16), (5, 17^18)` (72 negative clauses, width 5..7).
  - Side B pairs: `(9, 13), (10, 14), (11, 19^20), (12, 21^22)` (36 negative clauses, width 4..6).
  - Cross clauses: 42 positive clauses (width 4..6), replacing `-q` with `(-u, v), (u, -v)` and `+q` with `(u, v), (-u, -v)` for each XOR pair `q = u^v`.
- **Why `compress_root` succeeds and forces the worst-case order**:
  - `max_block_width = 7 <= 8`, total `space = 3552 <= 16384`, `verification_work` is ~1.4e5 `<= 8e6`, and `15..22` never appear in odd blocks (`14 < 22` frozen).
  - Every Side-A basis form appears in `16 + 4 = 20` blocks; every Side-B basis form appears in `8 + 5 = 13` blocks; every multi-form sum appears in at most 8 blocks.
  - Thus `compress_root`'s sort `(-freq, popcount, v)` deterministically selects all 18 independent basis forms in the exact order:
    `1..5` (`a1..a5`, freq 20, wt 1), `6..8` (`a1'..a3'`, freq 20, wt 1), `9..10` (`15^16, 17^18`, freq 20, wt 2), `11..14` (`b1..b4`, freq 13, wt 1), `15..16` (`b1'..b2'`, freq 13, wt 1), `17..18` (`19^20, 21^22`, freq 13, wt 2).
- **Why `core_refutation` returns UNKNOWN**:
  - On the original 150-clause input, every block of size 1, 2, or 4 is already a complete coset of its stabilizer, so `probe` removes 0 clauses (`no_clauses_removed`). On the 68-clause quotient, every block has size 1 (`no_clauses_removed`).
- **Residual growth trace on ascending quotient order `1..18` (distinguishing growth from skip)**:
  - Compression succeeds; there is no discovery failure.
  - Layers 1–3 (`1, 2, 3`): `2 -> 4 -> 8` states. No variable satisfies `pos * neg <= pos + neg`, and all UP-filtered width-<=5 windows have full-rank `Z^k` hulls.
  - Layer 4 (`4`): All 16 assignments to `(1, 2, 3, 4)` leave `a5` with `neg = 1`. The all-True branch (`TTTT`) emits unit clauses `(-5), (-10)` and collapses to UNSAT. For each of the remaining **15** nonempty subsets `S <= {6, 7, 8, 9}`, `elim` eliminates `5` and `10` to produce `(-S, B_j)` alongside `(s, B_j)` for `s in S`, then halts (`pos = 4, neg = 4`, `16 > 8`). All 15 states are pairwise incomparable under `below(g, h)` (different active singleton sets `S` and incomparable `(-S, B_j)` clauses), and no pairwise clause union forms a 5-variable window containing two complete B-pairs plus a 5th B-variable, so `IALH-5` returns `UNKNOWN` on all 15 states (**peak = 15**).
  - Layers 5–9 (`5, 6, 7, 8, 9`): variable `5` is already eliminated (15 retained), then `6, 7, 8, 9` collapse `15 -> 7 -> 3 -> 1 -> 0` (UNSAT) with heavy `@lru_cache` reuse (~65 total IALH-5 calls, fewer root windows than Neon58: 100 vs 112).

This is a finite growth fixture demonstrating larger residual branching (predicted peak 15 vs Neon58's 8) after successful Lean-checkable compression; it is not an asymptotic lower bound proof.
